scope: Read-only Core application access and scheduler inspection

unix_identities.source: Live id and getent passwd through the existing master SSH session

correction.reason: The distinct login names map to the same Unix UID/GID; name inequality did not establish different ownership.

next_action: Await explicit approval to enable application SSH, then verify the existing login executes as UID 1004 and test scoped owner-preserving file operations outside the live webroot.
limitations: Matching account UID is not proof of successful shell authentication or deployment access.
Enabling application SSH does not pause the nine Core jobs owned by the separate master user.
The current maintenance host adapter handles only its own user's crontab; using it as the application owner alone would not hold the master-user schedule.
No installed Supervisord and an empty application schedule do not prove that all running, external or system-level writers are absent.
